title: Runtime & Ratings
text:
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

films = pd.read_csv("films.csv")
This page compares film runtimes with IMDb ratings. In Figure 1, each point represents one film.
plt.scatter(films["runtime_min"], films["imdb_rating"])
plt.xlabel("Runtime (minutes)")
plt.ylabel("IMDb rating (0–10)")
plt.show()







Figure 1: Film runtime in minutes and IMDb rating

title: Budget and Revenue
text:
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

films = pd.read_csv("films.csv")

This page compares film production budgets with worldwide revenues. In Figure 1, each point represents one film, with both amounts measured in millions of US dollars.

plt.scatter(films["budget_musd"], films["revenue_musd"])
plt.xlabel("Production budget (millions of US dollars)")
plt.ylabel("Worldwide revenue (millions of US dollars)")
plt.show()







Figure 1: Production budget and worldwide revenue, in millions of US dollars

title: The Bond Films
text:
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

films = pd.read_csv("films.csv")

bond = films[films["franchise"] == "James Bond"]
bond = bond.sort_values("year")

The Bond films in this dataset run from 1995 to 2021.

plt.plot(bond["year"], bond["revenue_musd"])
plt.xlabel("Release year")
plt.ylabel("Worldwide revenue (millions of US dollars)")
plt.show()







Figure 1: Worldwide revenue of James Bond films over time.

title: Box Office Numbers
text: This website explores 104 well-known films released between 1980 and 2025. The dataset includes film titles, franchises, budgets, worldwide revenues, runtimes, and IMDb ratings. Financial figures are approximate, measured in millions of US dollars, and not adjusted for inflation.
